faqs.q: Sec. 98-103. - Issuance of sales tax revenue securities.
faqs.a:
(a)
Pursuant to the authority of section
11.5.5
of the Charter, the city may from time-to-time, and at any time, issue sales tax
               revenue securities as set forth therein. Sales tax revenue securities may be issued
               in one or more series and may bear such date, be payable upon demand or mature at
               such time, bear interest at such rate, be in such denomination, be in such form, either
               coupon or registered or otherwise, carry such conversion or registration privileges,
               have such rank or priority, be executed in such manner, be payable in such medium
               of payment, be payable at such place, be subject to such callability provisions or
               terms of redemption (with or without premiums), be of such description, contain or
               be subject to such covenants, provisions, terms, conditions and agreements (including
               provisions concerning events of default), and have such other characteristics as may
               be determined by the city council of the city and which are not inconsistent with
               the Charter.
(b)
The city council of the city may, subject to the limitations set forth in
section 98-101
and the Charter, pledge all or any portion, however determined, or any combination,
               of the sales and use tax proceeds derived under this article to the payment of sales
               tax revenue securities.
(c)
Sales tax revenue securities may be issued for any purpose for which city securities
               may be issued by the city, including, but not limited to, for the purpose of the making
               of one or more loans to, or for the purpose of purchasing one or more obligations
               of, the city urban renewal authority, or any other urban renewal authority from time-to-time
               organized and existing within the city, under such terms and conditions as the city
               council may approve and which are not inconsistent with the Charter.
(Code 1981, § 31-72; Ord. No. 3783, § 2, 12-16-2002)
